title: Outlook for iOS and Android: Purview label inheritance from email attachments
summary: Hold: the briefing calls the required licence tier unpublished even though its cited service description states a requirement for automatic or policy-based labeling. It also locates label priority in a publishing policy, whereas Microsoft defines it through the Information Protection Labels list. The portal paths and PowerShell calls are supported, and the briefing correctly reports the disagreement about mobile availability.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes Outlook for iOS and Android applying or recommending an email sensitivity label from labeled attachments according to organizational policy.
claims.quote: When users attach files with sensitivity labels, Outlook can automatically apply or recommend an email sensitivity label based on organizational policy settings.

claims.claim: The roadmap says inheritance reduces manual labeling effort.
claims.quote: This helps organizations maintain consistent data classification and protection while reducing manual labeling effort.

claims.quote: Searched: '"Outlook" "iOS" "inheritance" "policy" automatically attachments'; read Configure label inheritance from email attachments in sensitivity-labels-office-apps. It refers to the capabilities table and does not name iOS or Android.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether an already-enabled inheritance policy takes effect on mobile without further action.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Outlook iOS Android attachment label inheritance existing policy AttachmentAction automatic rollout licensing meter'; opened Office apps, versions, create-sensitivity-labels and Set-LabelPolicy. No mobile transition instructions for already-enabled policies were found.

claims.claim: No checked source says rollout changes behavior for tenants that have not selected the inheritance checkbox.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Outlook" "iOS" "inheritance" "policy" automatically attachments'; read the roadmap record and Office apps inheritance section. They describe policy-based behavior and turning inheritance on, not changing an unselected checkbox during rollout.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Purview service description has no separate feature row for label inheritance from email attachments.
claims.quote: Searched: '"label inheritance" "attachments" licensing E5'; searched the fetched Purview service description for inherit and attachment and read its sensitivity labeling tables. No separate email-attachment inheritance row appears.

claims.claim: The licence tier required for this policy-based inheritance setting is not yet published because the service description has no dedicated row.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy‑based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).
claims.fix: Replace the sentence beginning 'The service description has no row' with 'The service description states that automatic or policy-based sensitivity labeling requires Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG); it lists no separate row for attachment inheritance.' Remove the licence-tier question from Open questions. The existing cited Purview service description supplies this wording.

claims.claim: The capability is included within the named qualifying sensitivity-labeling licences rather than a separately documented feature purchase.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy‑based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.claim: No feature-specific consumption meter is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: '"label inheritance" attachments pricing meter billing'; opened the Purview service description, Office apps inheritance section and purview-billing-models. No meter for Outlook email attachment inheritance is listed.

claims.claim: Learn's setting description does not name a separate inheritance switch for iOS or Android.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Outlook iOS Android disable attachment label inheritance separate mobile switch AttachmentAction Set-LabelPolicy'; read the Office apps inheritance section and Set-LabelPolicy AttachmentAction reference. Neither names a separate mobile inheritance switch.

claims.claim: Label priority order in the label policy decides which attachment label wins.
claims.quote: When you create your sensitivity labels in the Microsoft Purview portal, they appear in a list on the Labels page from Information Protection. In this list, the order of the labels is important because it sets their priority.
claims.fix: Replace 'Label priority order in your label policy decides which label wins.' with 'The highest priority eligible attachment label wins.' This preserves the inheritance behavior already documented by the cited Office apps page without incorrectly locating label priority inside a publishing policy.
